terms.meaning: the row of buttons at the bottom of the screen that switches between the main sections
the address of a screen in the app, usually taken from its file name
the shared file of colors, fonts and spacing used by all screens

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the tab bar
sections.what: Brings in the tab component, the icon set and the theme colors that the tab bar uses.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the parts the tab bar needs to draw itself.

sections.name: TAB_ICONS
sections.title: Icon pairs for each tab
sections.what: Lists the icon each tab uses when selected and when not selected, keyed by the tab's route name.
sections.why: Gives each tab a filled icon when active and an outline icon when inactive, a common pattern for tab bars.
sections.watch_out: The keys must match the tab file names exactly. A mismatch leaves that tab without an icon.

sections.name: TabLayout
sections.title: Tab bar layout and the five tabs
sections.what: Builds the bottom bar with dark styling, sets the active and inactive label colors, and lists the five tabs with their titles. The chat tab is titled Maate AI.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fixed height and bottom padding leave room for the phone's home bar. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The bar height and padding are fixed numbers, so a change here affects every tab screen.

summary: Sets up the five-tab bottom navigation bar that the main sections of the app sit behind.
purpose: Defines the bottom tabs for Home, Timeline, Reminders, Maate AI and Profile, including their icons, labels and colors.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the choice of five tabs. The list matches the screen files in the tabs folder.
how: Loads the navigation library, the icon set and the theme colors. Each tab gets an icon pair from the icon map, a title, and shared styling for the bar and its text. The five tabs are then listed in order.
inputs: The route name of each tab screen, the theme colors and fonts, and the icon map.
outputs: A bottom navigation bar shown on every tab screen. No data is returned or saved.
risks: Renaming a tab file without updating the icon map leaves that tab with no icon. The bar height is fixed at 88 pixels, which can look cramped or too tall on some phones.
debug: If a tab icon is missing, compare the icon map keys with the file names in the tabs folder. If the bar overlaps content or looks cut off, check the height and bottom padding values.
